summaryForMax:
Feature-to-outcome line: this closes the gap from your inc3b UAT verbatim ("when I move that radius slider to the right, I want to see the planet on my screen get bigger"). Unit layer (spine-conformance AC-0, mapping shape AC-VIS-MONO, LOD re-keying AC-LOD-KEY, display-only fence AC-ZERO-CLOBBER, staging-doc AC-STAGE-DOC) is PASS — independently re-run: 23/23 new tests, golden byte-identical (40c18aad), full suite exactly at the pre-existing 4-failure baseline, zero denylist hits. Integration layer (AC-SCALE-LIVE, AC-CLAMP, AC-OVERLAY) is PASS — driven live on :5175 at commit 5cef327 with console clean; I spot-checked the screenshots myself and the disc visibly grows (~80px at 0.5 RE to ~250px+ at 8 RE) with no clipping at min-zoom and overlays/rivers tracking the disc surface.

What's left is AC-UAT, and only you can close it. To render your verdict: open the lab at http://localhost:5175/planet-lod-lab.html (dev server, or start it if it's not already up), pick the Rocky (Earthlike) preset, and drag the radius slider through increasing values (e.g. 0.5 -> 2 -> 8) — the planet disc on screen should visibly get bigger at each step, at a fixed camera-wheel position. Then switch to the Moon/Mercury (impact-airless) preset and click "New planet (re-roll both)" a couple of times — the disc size should visibly shift because each reroll draws a different radius. Two things to judge alongside that: (1) the known, in-contract non-goal — craters/terrain features scale WITH the disc (they do NOT get relatively smaller on a bigger world; the size cue is the disc itself, not shrinking craters) — carried into this build verbatim from inc3b; (2) an R1 side-effect flagged in BUILD-NOTES: at non-1 radius, live relief amplitude and cloud specks shift with apparent size (intended as "detail tracks apparent size") — worth a look alongside the main slider check since it's part of the same increment. If either of those doesn't read right to you, that's a UAT finding, not a bug in what was built to spec.
